notes: Canonical file written by this id's own initial research (2026-09-09) after reading the one proposal that created it, `from-tic-monthly-2027-01-19`, now shadowed. WHAT THIS RELEASE IS: the preliminary Report on Foreign Portfolio Holdings of U.S. Securities at end-June 2026 — the benchmark survey whose 2025 edition put foreign holdings at $35.3tn (shl2025r.pdf, April 2026) against $30.9tn in 2024 (shl2024r.pdf). THE PROPOSAL'S PREMISE IS NARROWED, NOT CONFIRMED. It was proposed on the ground that the survey benchmark is what makes February/March monthly vintages the largest restatements in the whole TIC panel. Half of that is mechanically impossible: the February MONTHLY release publishes on the 11th business day plus 0-3 days and the survey on the last business day of the same month, so the monthly vintage always precedes the survey — minimum gap 7 calendar days, computed over every February from 2003 to 2050, with no exception possible. A February vintage can therefore never carry this survey, which removes the panel's single largest restatement ($745.9bn, 2024-02) from the survey's account entirely. Treasury's own note (d) puts the survey-into-March convention in the PAST TENSE ('Before September 2011... usually released in March to include preliminary data from the annual survey'), replaced for Major Foreign Holders by note (c)'s Jan/Apr/Jul/Oct schedule since December 2011. The one feedback path Treasury still documents in the present tense is the QUARTERLY GROSS EXTERNAL DEBT release on the last business day of June, whose revisions 'include the results of the Survey of Foreign Holdings of U.S. Securities at end-June of the previous year' — proposed here as a separate entry. Impact LOW and symbols empty on the standing grounds (16:00 ET is after the equity cash close, the data is eight months stale at publication, no house playbook is macro-keyed). Additionally measured this session: the next session after a preliminary survey is statistically indistinguishable from any other month-end session (4.96bp vs 5.11bp mean |delta-10Y|, p=0.85, n=24 back to 2003) — month-end itself is the noisy thing (5.11bp vs 4.27bp for an ordinary session, p=0.002), and the survey adds nothing to it. Nothing here licenses an entry.
